anya: quick follow-up to the RFC thread — proposing an iterative carve‑out plan for the monolithic runtime control plane. idea is small, reversible slices, not a big bang.
kevin: high level — 👍. can you sketch the phases? what do we own after first slice?
maria: curious about data migrations. can we avoid schema blocks for teams?
anya: phases I have in mind: 1) discovery + read-only extract (adapter reads against monolith), 2) extract control APIs (write paths still proxied), 3) dual-write + migration for small tables, 4) rolling cutover with feature flag, 5) cleanup and delete. each phase targets one bounded responsibility (e.g., routing policies, quota bookkeeping, model-profile registry).
dana: sounds reasonable. low blast radius if each slice is small. how do we prevent getter/putter drift between proxy and new service?
anya: plan is to keep the proxy as a thin facade during phase 2 and add a compatibility adapter in the new service. add contract tests and golden prompts for behavior parity.
kevin: dual-write is always tricky. proposal: dual-write + read-after-write from new service during migration window, with an idempotency token to reconcile races.
maria: for data migration we can use a gradual reconciliation job (async) and mark records with a migration version column. avoids downtime.
anya: example migration command I imagine:```bash
./migrate-records --batch-size=500 --from=monolith-db --to=carved-db --dry-run
```
dana: feature flags + traffic split — recommend per-org canary (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%) with automatic rollback if latency or error budget breached.
kevin: add SLO gates: 95th latency <= baseline*1.3 and error rate delta < 0.1% for 30m window. infra team should produce a playbook for rollback.
infra-bot: deploy-checker: new service image build succeeded (sha: abc123). integration-tests: 44/47 passed, 3 flaky tests flagged.
maria: observability notes: we need request tracing across facade -> new service -> storage. also per-route tokenized cost breakdown (to detect cost regressions). I can produce dashboards.
anya: good call. also need rollout checklist: schema toggles, feature flag rollout plan, canary org list, metrics & alerting thresholds, migration runbook, post-cutover cleanups.
dana: security: ensure KMS keys are accessible for both systems during migration, and audit logs keep both sides for x weeks.
kevin: one more ops detail: during phase 3 dual-write, how do we handle transactional invariants? some ops expect strong consistency.
anya: for strict invariants we keep the monolith as the source of truth until we can guarantee transactional parity; carve out only eventual-consistent components first (routing decisions, caching layers). leave session/stateful engines for later.
maria: volunteers for telemetry & dashboards: I will own metrics and SLO dashboards for the cutover window.
kevin: I'll pair on migration scripts and reconciliation jobs.
dana: I'll own rollout automation and feature-flag gating.
anya: thanks — I'll draft the follow-up RFC with sequence, expected PRs, test plan, and a migration checklist. tagging the infra team for an initial risk review.
kevin: please include a short failure-mode table in the RFC (what we do if reconciliation falls behind, if dual-write diverges, etc).
anya: will do. aiming to have draft up by EOD Friday. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
infra-bot: reminder: weekly-arch-sync scheduled Thu 10:00 — add this as agenda item.
